issues.description: The supplied SAS program names a separate “DLM Data - CPIS and Zucman” producer for `dlm.dlm_full_matrices_keyvars`, but that program and matrix are absent from this PDF-only package. The selected supplied-code target can start from a compatible author-prepared matrix; only if the raw-rebuild alternative is chosen are CPIS Table 11, Netherlands SFI, OANDA FX and IMF IIP separate upstream input contracts. Their exact history/schema remains unclosed, so that alternative is not the selected mandatory input set.

All supplied SAS and Stata programs are embedded in a PDF; no standalone `.sas`, `.do`, or source data files are inventoried. Extract faithful working copies from the document and resolve any omitted setup before running; source text itself is not an executable path.

The main SAS library uses `[redacted-path-0a49898a8ce5]`; the separate Table 1 SAS section switches to `[redacted-path-c5b4dfd6e8e8]`; Stata changes to a third user Dropbox folder. The active main SAS code writes `dlm.data1`, while PROC EXPORT calls for data1, cpisfull, zucmanfull, dlm_hmt08 and dlm_hmt15 are all inside block comments. Configure distinct roots and a verified handoff. Active ODS TAGSETS.EXCELXP writes the separate Table 1 workbook.

The PDF-only package lacks directly consumed author tables and exact source-to-output manifests needed to validate fields, country mappings, units, cleaning and history. Each direct read, including the CPIS/Zucman matrix and countrycodes, has its own requirement. CPIS Table 11, Netherlands SFI, OANDA FX and IMF IIP belong only to the conditional raw-preparer route and can be bypassed by a compatible matrix.

The only bounded SAS startup checks failed before a SAS session could initialize TKELS. Base SAS procedures and active ODS TAGSETS.EXCELXP therefore remain unverified in this environment; the failure does not establish absent licensing. The Stata exports in the PDF are block-commented, so no active SAS-to-Stata export facility is required by the source.

evidence.description: The datasheet describes TIC, CPIS, Zucman inputs, Netherlands SFI, OANDA, IMF IIP and compiled top individual rates.
evidence.file: DLM datasheet.pdf
evidence.quote:
2. Data Sources
Most of the primary data collection for TIC and CPIS data was done in Spring 2016. The
calculations following Zucman [2013] were done in Summer 2017. Real estate, art, UCITS, Hong
Kong pension funds, and bitcoin data were collected between October 2017 and January 2019.
We used various data sources for our analysis:

1) TIC DATA (for inbound FPI tests)
   • Source: United States Treasury website (https://www.treasury.gov/resource-center/data-
      chart-center/tic/Pages/ticsec2.aspx)
   • We downloaded .csv files of all available data for our sample period. We then converted
      all files to SAS format for merging into one dataset. There was no manual entry at any
      point in the process.

2) CPIS DATA (for worldwide FPI tests)
   • Source: International Monetary Fund website (http://data.imf.org/?sk=B981B4E3-4E58-
      467E-9B90-9DE0C3367363&sId=1424963554286)
   • We downloaded Table 11 (Geographic Breakdown of Total Portfolio Investment Assets)
      for all available years. We then converted all files to SAS format for merging into one
      dataset. There was no manual entry at any point in the process.

3) ADJUSTED CPIS AND ZUCMAN GAP DATA:
   We used the downloaded CPIS data to calculate these measures. To do so, we followed the
   code posted by Gabriel Zucman (http://gabriel-zucman.eu/) and updated the code accordingly
   for our sample period.
   Sources:
   • Netherlands SFI data: https://www.dnb.nl/en/statistics/statistics-dnb/balance-of-
        payments-and-international-investment-position/index.jsp
   • Exchange rates from www.oanda.com
   • IMF International Investment Position (IIP) data: http://data.imf.org/?sk=7A51304B-
        6426-40C0-83DD-CA473CA1FD52&sId=1409773422141

4) TAX RATE DATA:
   • We obtain the top statutory individual tax rate in each country-year. As no single source
      had complete data, we compile our dataset from the University of Michigan, the OECD,
      KPMG, the Tax Foundation, and Trading Economics.

5) WORLD BANK DATA:
   • We use the following data items from the World Bank to construct control variables:
     1. Government effectiveness – from Worldwide Governance Indicators Project
     2. Population
     3. Gross Domestic Product
     4. Number of mobile phone subscriptions per 100 people

6) MATCHING:
   •  All datasets are merged using country ISO codes and year.

8) REAL ESTATE DATA:
   We compiled several sources for the country-year values of the global house price index (real
   and nominal), housing rents, and disposable income per person. Sources:
   • Economist (2017), “Global House Prices” (https://www.economist.com/blogs
      /graphicdetail/2017/03/daily-chart-6) accessed on April 18, 2018
   • OECD (2018), “Prices: Analytical house price indicators”, Main Economic Indicators
      database (http://dx.doi.org/10.1787/cbcc2905-en) accessed on April 18, 2018
   • Bank for International Settlements, Residential Property Prices from FRED, Federal
      Reserve Bank of St. Louis (https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/QHUN628BIS) accessed on
      April 26, 2018.

evidence.description: The datasheet names Swiss-Impex, Geneva Freeport materials and EFAMA UCITS reports.
evidence.file: DLM datasheet.pdf
evidence.quote:
9) ART MARKET DATA:
   • Source: Swiss Federal Customs Administration FCA website, the Swiss-Impex.
      https://www.gate.ezv.admin.ch/swissimpex/. Cite originally accessed in August 2017 and
      again accessed in April, May, and June 2018.
   • Source: Geneva Freeport Financial Statements and Powerpoint Presentation from June
      2016. http://geneva-freeports.ch/en/ Cite originally accessed in January 2019.

10) UCITS DATA:
    • Source: European Fund and Asset Management Association, publications of European
       Quarterly Statistical Releases. This page includes reports from 2011 to 2017.
